panels.text: A Jacquard machine is controlled by a "chain of cards": punched cards laced together into a continuous sequence. Joseph Marie Jacquard patented it in 1804.
Multiple rows of holes are punched on each card, and one complete card corresponds to one row of the design.
A portrait of Jacquard, woven in silk on a Jacquard loom, required 24,000 punched cards.
Charles Babbage owned one of these portraits. It inspired him in using perforated cards in his Analytical Engine.
